card.name: Words just before a threat or competition
card.fires_on: Small linking words or verbs (have, as, in, not, foreign) placed where the next word is likely to be about competition, threat or rivalry. Mostly in general web text about industries, religions or markets.

modes.label: Viewing something as a threat
modes.description: The word "as" after a verb like view or regard, just before a threat or hindrance.
modes.example: The U.S. shouldn't view this<< as>> a threat but rather an opportunity for greater

modes.label: New rivals changing a market
modes.description: A verb or modifier after a subject describing new alternatives, imports or outside players that compete.
modes.example: The textile industry met falling prices and increasing American and<< foreign>> competition with improved automation in the mills.

modes.label: Interaction or substitution phrases
modes.description: Linking words in clauses about substitutes or interacting with other things.
modes.example: Producers who seek to maximize long-term revenue will want to maintain oil prices stable at the highest price that does not induce substantial investment<< in>> substitutes,

card.writes: It pushes the model toward words meaning threat, competition and competing.
card.plain: It fires on little words right before the text is likely to say something is a threat or a competitor.
